Note::TexAccessor::to_html¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::to_html() const

Convert A Recognized TeX Subset To HTML Markup¶

to_html() rewrites a fixed set of common TeX commands to their HTML equivalents — headings, bold, italic/emphasis, a linebreak, and list items — unwraps color and hyperlink wrappers down to their visible content, and removes labels, references, citations, packages, bibliography commands, spacing/delimiter commands, and font-size declarations. Use it for a quick, best-effort HTML preview of simple TeX prose; it is not a full document converter.

The recognized rewrites, applied in this order:

TeX

HTML

\section{...} / \section*{...}

<h1>...</h1>

\subsection{...} / \subsection*{...}

<h2>...</h2>

\subsubsection{...} / \subsubsection*{...}

<h3>...</h3>

\textbf{...}

<strong>...</strong>

\emph{...} / \textit{...}

<em>...</em>

\\ (a TeX linebreak)

<br/>

\item

<li>

\textcolor{...}{...}/\colorbox{...}{...} and \href{url}{label}/ hyperref commands are then unwrapped down to their visible content — the color name and the URL are both discarded, same as on to_markdown; to_html() does not emit an HTML anchor for a hyperlink, it only keeps the label text.

There is no mode parameter — unlike to_text and to_markdown’s own mode, to_html() has exactly one behavior.

The operation is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note. Undefined input remains undefined; Bool, Int64, Float64, and Bytes receivers are rejected because TeX source is Text.

Example 1: Headings, Inline Formatting, Linebreak, Item, Link, And Color¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({
    R"(\section{Intro}\subsection{Detail}\subsubsection{Fine})",
    R"(\textbf{Bold} and \emph{emphasis}\\next \item first)",
    R"(See \href{https://example.test}{label} \label{x} \ref{x}.)",
    R"(\textcolor{red}{warn})"})
    .tex().to_html()
    << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["<h1>Intro</h1><h2>Detail</h2><h3>Fine</h3>", "<strong>Bold</strong> and <em>emphasis</em><br/>next <li> first", "See label .", "warn"]

The third cell shows the link unwrapped to its bare label — the URL is discarded, not turned into an <a href="..."> tag — alongside the two recognized removals, \label{x} and \ref{x}. The fourth cell shows \textcolor{red}{warn} reduced to its bare content the same way.

Example 2: A 2-D Grid, Shape Preserved¶

const auto grid = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(\section{A})", R"(\textbf{B})", "plain", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << grid.tex().to_html() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["<h1>A</h1>", "<strong>B</strong>"], 
  ["plain", ""]
]

Example 3: Undefined And Non-Text Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().to_html().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2}).tex().to_html();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "to html Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
to html Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • to_markdown: the equivalent conversion to Markdown, which shares the same color/hyperlink removal and adds a mode for case-folding that to_html() has no counterpart for.

  • to_text: drop TeX structure entirely instead of converting it to another markup language.

  • render: a readable Unicode projection instead of markup.
